title: E-commerce Search via Content Collaborative Graph Neural Network

problem.claim: E-commerce search models increasingly use Graph Neural Networks.

gap.claim: Existing approaches lack proper product-content semantics, are inefficient for industry-scale graphs, and are less accurate for long-tail queries and cold-start products.

contributions.claim: CC-GNN enables content phrases to participate explicitly in graph propagation to capture phrase meaning and semantic drift.
CC-GNN introduces scalable graph-learning components including efficient graph construction, MetaPath-guided Message Passing, and Difficulty-aware Representation Perturbation.
CC-GNN uses Counterfactual Data Supplement in supervised and contrastive learning to address long-tail and cold-start problems.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe CC-GNN as a novel Content Collaborative Graph Neural Network.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On a real e-commerce dataset with 100-million-scale nodes, CC-GNN reportedly improves several key metrics by more than 10% for overall, long-tail, and cold-start cases while reducing computational complexity.
The proposed components reportedly improve different recommendation models on a public dataset.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph Neural Networks are widely used for e-commerce search.
Existing methods have semantic, scalability, long-tail, and cold-start limitations.
CC-GNN addresses these limitations through content-aware propagation, scalable graph learning, and counterfactual data supplementation.
Experiments report improvements on large real and public datasets, including reduced computational complexity and transfer across recommendation models.

source_observation.claim: Explicitly incorporating content phrases into graph propagation is reported to address product-content semantic representation.

interpretation.claim: Graph-based search models may benefit when semantic content units participate directly in relational computation.

application.claim: Consider content-aware propagation for search or recommendation graphs with phrase-level semantic gaps.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach helps outside the reported datasets and tasks.

source_observation.claim: Counterfactual data supplementation is reported for long-tail queries and cold-start products.

interpretation.claim: Synthetic or counterfactual training data may mitigate sparse supervision in underrepresented query or product cases.

application.claim: Evaluate counterfactual supplementation when search or recommendation data contain long-tail or cold-start sparsity.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the counterfactual construction or its behavior under different data distributions.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset name, baseline identities, metric names, statistical details, or ablation results.
The abstract does not specify implementation details for the proposed components or quantify each component's individual effect.
